Remark. q-deformed nuclear and atomic models (\mathrm{SU}_q(2) rotor, q-oscillator, Elliott \mathrm{SU}(3))

Remark (relation to q-deformed nuclear and atomic models).

The magic-number result of conj:magic-numbers-from-q joins several quantum-algebraic accounts of nuclear shell structure. We separate our mechanism from three strands of the quantum-group literature. In previous models, the deformation parameter is fitted to the data. In our framework, the substrate parameter q_0 \approx 1.10998 is categorically extracted (not a free parameter) and calibrated via the neutron β-sector bar-skew channel.

\mathrm{SU}_q(2) rotor bands

The \mathrm{SU}_q(2) rotator model [minkov1996] describes the rotational bands of deformed rare-earth and actinide nuclei. Its Hamiltonian is proportional to the second Casimir of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), with spectrum

  E_I = \frac{1}{2\vartheta}\,[I]_q\,[I+1]_q + E_0,

where \vartheta is a moment-of-inertia parameter and [\,x\,]_q is a q-number. The deformation is a phase q = e^{i\varphi} with |q| = 1. The q-number [I]_q = \sin(\varphi I)/\sin\varphi yields an oscillatory spectrum. The parameter \varphi is fitted per band. This per-band fit is where the variable moment of inertia enters: \varphi tracks the centrifugal stretching of each rotational band (in the rotator model it is tied to the valence-pair number), so the deformation is a soft, nucleus-dependent softness parameter rather than a single constant. A fixed q_0 therefore does not "absorb" the moment-of-inertia variation — in this model that variation is carried by the per-band fit of \varphi, not by one derived constant, and the claim that a single q captures the stretching is phenomenological curve-fitting, not a fixed-constant derivation. This Casimir matches def:q-angular-momentum, but evaluates on a different analytic branch. Our substrate q_0 is real and greater than 1, yielding a hyperbolic q-number. We share the Casimir operator, but avoid the fitted phase.

q-deformed harmonic oscillator

A three-dimensional q-deformed harmonic oscillator with \mathfrak{u}_q(3) \supset \mathfrak{so}_q(3) symmetry [raychev1998] reproduces shell closures by level filling. Expanding the energy in the deformation yields a term proportional to \ell(\ell+1). This orbit-orbit correction reproduces the cluster magic numbers 2, 8, 20, 40, 58, 92, \dots. It does not produce the spin-orbit (\ell \cdot s) coupling required for the nuclear ladder 28, 50, 82, 126. A scalar oscillator carries no spin degree of freedom. The \ell \cdot s term must be supplied by coupling an external spin-\tfrac{1}{2}, matching the Mayer–Jensen shell model [mayer1955]. The q-deformation yields the orbit-orbit term, while the spin-orbit input remains independent.

Elliott \mathrm{SU}(3)

Elliott's \mathrm{SU}(3) classification [elliott1958] maps harmonic-oscillator shells to \mathrm{SU}(3) irreducible representations. It is an undeformed (q = 1) organizing symmetry. It does not serve as the classical limit of our mechanism. The magic-number signal of conj:magic-numbers-from-q is a genuinely q-deformed coherence effect that vanishes at q = 1. Elliott's \mathrm{SU}(3) and the many-body Hecke trace are complementary accounts at opposite ends of the deformation axis.

The complementarity is, more precisely, the two sides of the quantum Schur–Weyl duality of prop:shell-schur-weyl-self-duality: on (\mathbb{C}^3)^{\otimes n} the mutual-centralizer pair is \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_3) \times H_n(q). The many-body Hecke trace reads binding off the H_n(q) factor (partitions \lambda \vdash n), while Elliott's \mathrm{SU}(3) is the q = 1 image of the \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_3) factor; the pair degenerates to the classical \mathrm{GL}(3) \times S_n centralizer duality at q = 1. This duality is an algebraic identity at every q, so it coexists with — rather than contradicts — the magic-number signal being a genuinely q \neq 1 coherence effect: the commutant structure holds throughout, and only the coherence that sharpens the shell gaps vanishes in the q \to 1 limit.

q-deformed atomic Aufbau

A parallel construction organizes the atomic table rather than the nuclear shells. The q-deformed Aufbau principle of Négadi and Kibler [negadi1992] builds the electron filling order from the deformed dynamical-symmetry chain \mathrm{SO}(4) \supset \mathrm{SO}_q(3), reproducing the Madelung (n + \ell, n) ordering for atoms and monoatomic ions. There q is a deformation parameter of the symmetry chain, imposed to organize the ordering — not derived from an underlying constant. This is the fixed-versus-free distinction of the nuclear models above, transposed to the atomic sector: our q_0 \approx 1.10998 is one substrate constant, fixed by the calibration triple and shared by every atom and nucleus, whereas a q-Aufbau deformation is a per-scheme organizing parameter with no substrate derivation. The atomic magic numbers here are read from the same many-body Hecke trace at that single q_0 (via conj:magic-numbers-from-q), not from a separately deformed atomic symmetry.

The common distinction

In these previous models, the deformation is a free parameter fitted to the observable. The present framework fixes q_0 once and reads the magic numbers off the many-body Hecke trace. The reproduction of higher nuclear or atomic shells without tuning is a forward test. The homological route of rem:k12-barrier-bypass supplies the parameter-free prediction at 50, 82, 126.
